result.title: 3D Neural Rendering for Automated Ultrasonic Laser Scans
result.summary: Laser doppler vibrometer (LDV) scans can be used to detect defects and cracks in manufactured parts before they are deployed. This work presents a method for reconstructing the steady-state surface wavefield of a three-dimensional part by combining automated robotic manipulation with neural rendering. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator (UFactory xArm6) with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presented an acoustically excited test article to a stationary LDV at a sequence of known orientations, yielding a set of complex-valued 2D scans with poses derived analytically from the arm kinematics rather than from image-based pose estimation. These scans were used to train a novel complex-nerfacto model, a modified Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) pipeline that replaces the standard three-channel RGB output head with a two-channel output. Complex-nerfacto represents the real and imaginary velocity components of a wavefield, preserving the complex measurement without quantization. Reconstructions of a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket were evaluated against measured scans using Z-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC). The complex-valued pipeline achieved a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto model trained on rendered images of the same data. The resulting surface wavefield reconstructions supported defect detection and characterization on complex components. We identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用六自由度机械臂在已知位姿下向固定的激光多普勒测振仪呈现被测件，得到多角度复数扫描，并训练输出实部/虚部双通道的 complex-nerfacto，重建三维稳态表面波场，留出视角平均 ZNCC 为 0.60（RGB 基线为 0.28），用于焊缝缺陷检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其复数隐式场以双通道无量化地保留连续测量状态，配合机器人主动采集已知位姿的多视角证据，可能为 LVR 中「连续证据如何留在内部状态」与「下一步看哪里」的证据筛选问题提供类比线索，但与 VLM 推理无直接关系，需较多核查。
